stage_a.note: Wendy delivers the pitch with a huge, persistent smile and an extremely upbeat, cheerful tone.
She shows pronounced, sustained excitement about her gnomes and the joy they bring to customers.
She is highly approachable and friendly, addressing the panel with clear affection and warmth.

venture.description: Hand-crafted, customizable decorative gnomes for various occasions and holidays.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy presents Wendy's Gnome Shop, seeking $200k for 20%, explaining the decorative gnomes and custom design options.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks what a gnome is used for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy says she designed custom gnomes for each shark.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori says she does not have one.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin points out his gnome has a crown.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy says Barbara gets to experience the design-a-gnome process.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara jokes about having to work for her gnome.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy notes Barbara gets to pick it out herself.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara says that is good.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks what people use the gnomes for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy explains they are placed around the home to make people smile.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy asks Barbara to choose an embellishment for her gnome's hat.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara chooses the sunflower embellishment.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy asks Barbara to choose a hat color and boots.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara selects a specific beard and a red hat.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy says it will take a few minutes to build and she is ready for questions.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks how she acquires customers who want to buy the gnomes.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy says 15% come from their website and 80% from Etsy.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks about the customer acquisition cost for her own website.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy states their customer acquisition cost is about $5.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks what it costs to buy a gnome.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy says the average price is about $35.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks what it costs to make one gnome.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy says it costs $3.50 for materials.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark compliments the great margins.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks if there are cheaper options available for someone who finds hers expensive.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy says her prices are comparable to others on Etsy.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks if people brush their gnomes.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy confirms they do and that they tell people to comb their gnome.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark jokes that it gives Kevin something to comb.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin repeats the phrase comb your gnome.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark expresses amazement that people pay $35 for the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy affirms that customers absolutely love them.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks to understand the overall market for gnomes.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark jokes about missing a recent study on the gnome market.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy explains people have an emotional connection with them and they make people smile.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks what her sales have been to date.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy says she has been in business 18 months with $688,000 in lifetime sales.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond expresses surprise at the sales figure.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori expresses surprise that people like gnomes that much.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin notes there must be many doll gnomes available online.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy acknowledges factory-produced competition but asserts her better quality and status as the top Etsy seller with 23,000 sold.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks to confirm she has sold that many.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy confirms she has.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks how she achieved nearly $700,000 in sales starting as a hobby 18 months ago.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy shares her story of starting the hobby after a breakup and spontaneously selling her first gnome on Etsy.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin jokes that the broken heart turned into cash flow.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark asks how much she invested to start and whether the business is profitable.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy says she started the business with less than $1,000.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark jokes about the massive return on her initial investment.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy adds they are profitable, netting $135,000 last year.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond acknowledges the profit figure.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks how many people work in the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy says she has three women working for her, plus her daughter.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Amber announces that Barbara's custom gnome is complete.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara expresses love for the completed gnome.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy hands the completed gnome to Barbara.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara says it is darling and she feels motherly toward it.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks Wendy about her professional background.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy explains she was a labor and delivery nurse and went to college at 35 to pursue it.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks Amber how she feels about what her mother has accomplished.

turns.speaker: F2
turns.summary: Amber expresses immense pride, noting they both retired from nursing to make gnomes.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin praises the incredible story and respects the sales figures.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin states he does not need a gnome in his portfolio and exits.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori praises the thriving business but says it is not right for her, exiting the deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark praises her as a shining example of turning a small investment into significant sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy agrees and expresses belief she can grow it much more.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark says it is a great niche business for her but not for him to invest in, and exits.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks where he or the others could add value to the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy says she needs a strategic partner with marketing and SEO expertise to scale and improve sourcing costs.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond offers $200k for 35% equity.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin jokes about the hair falling off the gnome.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond tells Wendy she is free to counter his offer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara asks if gnomes are a recent trend or if people have always liked them.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy says gnomes have been popular forever.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara asks about her high overhead, noting the $135,000 profit on $688,000 in sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy explains that Etsy fees account for a lot of it, which is why she wants to drive website traffic.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara offers $200k for 30% plus a $1 per gnome royalty, citing her experience moving businesses off Etsy.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin clarifies that Barbara is asking for a royalty.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara says she is calling it a buck a gnome, not a royalty.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy points out that a buck a gnome is indeed a royalty.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond revises his offer to $200k for 30% with a 50-cent royalty until repaid, then 30% equity.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara drops her royalty, revising her offer to a straight $200k for 30%.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin notes that Wendy now has a real competition going on between the sharks.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy acknowledges the competitive situation.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks Wendy what she is going to do.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy asks Daymond if he will match Barbara's offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks if she means the exact same terms.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara asks if Wendy is playing them against each other.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark supports Wendy, saying she should negotiate.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy says she is smart.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Mark agrees that she is smart.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond asks why they should keep negotiating against themselves.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy says the business is worth it and they will make a lot of money.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara asks what she expects to make and net in the current year.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy projects $750,000 in revenue and $150,000 in net profit for the year.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond calculates his potential return based on her profit projection.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy confirms his calculation is correct.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin notes that getting 25% of the capital back is not a bad deal for Daymond.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond revises his offer to match Barbara's, offering $200k for 30%.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara tries to interject, stating that is not where her head is at.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond calls Barbara rude for interrupting his thought.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara argues that reliance on outside websites is her enemy and she can help move sales in-house.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond counters by citing his success with Bombas selling direct, telling Wendy to pick one.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy counters both offers, asking for $200k for 25% equity.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Lori asks if she is making that counter to both Daymond and Barbara.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy confirms the counter is to both of them.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Barbara rejects the counter, saying she will not go that far.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond also rejects the counter.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin asks Wendy what she will do now that the counter is rejected.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Wendy accepts Daymond's offer of $200k for 30%.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Daymond celebrates the deal, calling her his gnomey.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Kevin congratulates Wendy on securing the deal.
